balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities attributable to the parent; non-controlling interests (NCI) is the slice of consolidated equity owned by outside shareholders; both are plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Seazen Group Limited: Seazen consolidates a listed A-share subsidiary (New Town Holdings, 601155.SS) that it does not wholly own, so NCI is roughly 42% of total equity — not a rounding item. Parent shareholders' equity, not the consolidated total, is what the DCF values.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • NCI's share of equity drifting, which changes how much of consolidated net income (and any dividend) actually belongs to Seazen Group's own shareholders

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Seazen Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Seazen Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Seazen Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Seazen Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Seazen Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Seazen Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Seazen Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

subsidiaryBuyback.title: Subsidiary share buyback (601155.SS)
subsidiaryBuyback.content:
New Town Holdings (601155.SS), Seazen's listed A-share subsidiary, runs its own on-market share repurchase program funded from its own cash.

For Seazen Group Limited: this is tracked separately from any Seazen Group (HK-listed parent) repurchase because it does not retire parent shares or change the parent's share count used in the DCF — it slightly raises Seazen's effective economic interest in the subsidiary (and so, over time, NCI's share of consolidated equity falls a little), rather than returning cash to Seazen Group's own shareholders.

What to watch:

  • Whether the buyback is large enough to meaningfully shift the parent's effective ownership of the subsidiary
  • Confusing this with capital returned to Seazen Group shareholders directly

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Seazen Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
